claims.text: The FDA label lists acute alcohol intake among agents that may increase phenytoin serum levels.
claims.quote: Drugs that may increase phenytoin serum levels Antiepileptic drugs Ethosuximide, felbamate, oxcarbazepine, methsuximide, topiramate Azoles Fluconazole, ketoconazole, itraconazole, miconazole, voriconazole Antineoplastic agents Capecitabine, fluorouracil Antidepressants Fluoxetine, fluvoxamine, sertraline Gastric acid reducing agents H 2 antagonists (cimetidine), omeprazole Sulfonamides Sulfamethizole, sulfaphenazole, sulfadiazine, sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim Other Acute alcohol intake

claims.text: The FDA label lists chronic alcohol abuse among agents that may decrease phenytoin serum levels.
claims.quote:
Drugs that may decrease phenytoin serum levels Antacids Antacids may affect absorption of phenytoin.
Calcium carbonate, aluminum hydroxide, magnesium hydroxide Prevention or Management : Phenytoin and antacids should not be taken at the same time of day Antineoplastic agents usually in combination Bleomycin, carboplatin, cisplatin, doxorubicin, methotrexate Antiviral agents Fosamprenavir, nelfinavir, ritonavir Antiepileptic drugs Carbamazepine, vigabatrin Other Chronic alcohol abuse

headline.text: The FDA label lists increased phenytoin levels with acute alcohol intake and decreased levels with chronic alcohol abuse.

reported.text: The label distinguishes opposite effects on phenytoin serum levels according to the pattern of alcohol use.
